title: Understanding the Structural and Functional Role of Poxvirus F17 Phosphoprotein
content: Poxviruses are unusual dsDNA viruses in that they replicate entirely in the cytoplasm of host cell using their own DNA replication and transcription machinery [1]. Due to this unusual mechanism of DNA replication, poxvirus DNA is particularly susceptible to host cell cytosolic DNA sensors like cGAS. In humans, the cGAS enzyme is known to recognize foreign dsDNA which activates the cGAS-STING pathway that stimulates production of Type-1 IFNs as an integral component of the host defense against pathogens [2,3]. To counteract this, poxviruses encode a wide array of innate immune antagonists that are expressed very early after virus entry and enable poxviruses to establish infection.
